 The Batman: Part II has faced another potential production delay. By the time Robert Pattinson returns as the Caped Crusader on the big screen, it will have been six years since Matt Reeves' The Batman opened in theaters. The highly anticipated follow-up has faced multiple delays, with release dates set between 2025 and 2027 before finally settling on Feb. 18, 2028.

 While principal photography on The Batman: Part II began in June 2026, filming was halted on October 5, 2026, as Matt Reeves stepped away to focus on a personal family matter. On Oct.15, it was reported that acclaimed director Steven Soderbergh volunteered to finish filming the sequel , with Reeves returning to finish the project during post-production. The Hollywood Reporter previously reported that filming on The Batman: Part II was "two-thirds" completed, though it appears the movie will continue filming into the new year.
 During an appearance on Virgin Radio UK's The Chris Evans Breakfast Show , actor Andy Serkis revealed that production on The Batman: Part II will run into 2027. The actor, who played Alfred Pennyworth in The Batman and is set to reprise his role in the sequel, confirmed he has not shot a single scene for the movie yet. Serkis, via World of Reel , said:
 "I have yet to portray Alfred in this one, because filming has been extended. So, immediately after Christmas we'll be going."
 On October 26, Robert Pattinson confirmed filming was set to resume in November 2026 , saying, "I think they’re in production already. And I’m starting in a couple of days." Despite filming being underway, Serkis's comment implies the film won't be completed before the production breaks for the Christmas holiday. Fortunately, The Batman: Part II isn't scheduled for release for another 14 months, meaning even if it wraps filming in February 2027, it will have a full year of post-production.

 Plot details on The Batman: Part II remain under wraps. In addition to Pattinson and Serkis, returning cast members include Jeffrey Wright as Commissioner Gordon, Colin Farrell as Oz Cobb/The Penguin, Jayme Lawson as Mayor Bella Reál, and Gil Perez-Abraham as GCPD officer Martinez. New additions include Sebastian Stan, Scarlett Johansson, Brian Tyree Henry, and Charles Dance. While some reports suggested Stan and Johansson were cast as Harvey and Gilda Dent, respectively, Matt Reeves, DC Studios, and Warner Bros. have not confirmed it.
 The filming delays for The Batman: Part II mirror those that happened on Reeves' first Batman movie. Filming on The Batman began in January 2020, but was shut down two months later due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Filming resumed in Sept. 2020, with production wrapping on Mar. 13, 2021. This delayed The Batman 's release from June 25, 2021, to Oct. 1, and finally to its March 4, 2022, release date.

 The delays to The Batman: Part II kept James Gunn and Peter Safran from moving forward with their plans for a DCU Batman film titled The Brave and the Bold . Gunn did not want to interfere with what Reeves was building with The Batman franchise or have two films centered on the Dark Knight released in the same year. The lack of any Batman movie in Warner Bros. slate is rumored to be a factor in David Ellison appointing Jeremy Latcham as the new head of DC Studios , taking over from James Gunn and Peter Safran on Dec. 1, 2026.
 This leaves the future of The Batman and subsequent sequels up in the air. The recent reports that Pattinson screen-tested for the role of James Bond in Amazon MGM's upcoming reboot suggest the actor's tenure as Batman could be over. Even though Matt Reeves has hinted at wanting to tell a Batman trilogy, the long gap between films might not be something the new leadership at Warner Bros. or DC Studios is willing to wait for.
